title: Elevator System
summary: Several lifts serve requests from floors and from inside the cars.
problem: Design the control software of a building with several elevators. People press up or down on a floor, then choose a destination inside the car.
functional: Handle a hall call (floor, direction) and a car call (destination floor)
Choose which elevator answers a hall call
Each elevator moves, stops at requested floors and opens its doors
nonFunctional: Requests should be served with low waiting time and without starving a floor
A scheduling change must not require changing the elevator class
deliverables: A class diagram (Mermaid or an uploaded image) with the relationships between classes
The responsibility of each class in a sentence
The design patterns you used and where, or why you used none
Optional: code for the central class and one method of each
hints: An elevator is a small state machine: idle, moving up, moving down, doors open.
The scheduler that picks an elevator is the part most likely to change: make it replaceable.
reference:
### Classes
`ElevatorController` (receives hall calls), `Elevator` (state, current floor, a sorted set of stops), `Request`, `Direction`, `Door`, `DispatchStrategy`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
  class ElevatorController {
    +hallCall(floor, direction)
    +setOutOfService(elevatorId)
  }
  class Elevator {
    state
    currentFloor
    upStops
    downStops
    +carCall(floor)
    +addStop(request)
    +step()
  }
  class Request {
    floor
    direction
  }
  class Direction {
    <<enumeration>>
    UP
    DOWN
    NONE
  }
  class Door {
    +open()
    +close()
  }
  class DispatchStrategy {
    <<interface>>
    +choose(elevators, request) Elevator
  }
  ElevatorController o-- Elevator
  ElevatorController --> DispatchStrategy
  ElevatorController ..> Request
  Elevator *-- Door
  Elevator --> Direction
  Request --> Direction
  DispatchStrategy <|.. NearestCarStrategy
  DispatchStrategy <|.. LeastLoadedStrategy
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> OutOfService: fault or maintenance
  OutOfService --> Idle: back in service
  Idle --> MovingUp: stop above
  Idle --> MovingDown: stop below
  MovingUp --> DoorsOpen: reached a stop
  MovingDown --> DoorsOpen: reached a stop
  DoorsOpen --> Idle: no more stops
  DoorsOpen --> MovingUp: stops above
  DoorsOpen --> MovingDown: stops below
```

### Why it works
- `DispatchStrategy` (nearest car, least loaded, SCAN-style) is a strategy chosen by the controller, so scheduling changes are isolated.
- Each elevator keeps up-stops and down-stops and serves the current direction first (the "elevator algorithm"), which avoids starvation.
- State is explicit, so out-of-service is a state that dispatch skips; when a car goes out of service its pending hall calls are given back to the controller to dispatch again, and the car is only taken out between stops with the doors closed.
- Hall calls, car calls and the movement loop run concurrently, so each elevator's stop sets are touched by one thread at a time (a lock, or one event loop per elevator). A nearest-car strategy can starve a far floor on a busy building; SCAN-style service inside each car and an age bonus in dispatch are common remedies.
- Hall calls go to the controller; car calls go straight to the elevator.
